tickets.title: Machine-wide running and queued counts in every statusline
tickets.what: Spec §5 M2. The work-summary snapshot (`src/collectors/work-summary-snapshot.ts:22-35,71-84`) publishes machine-wide `running` and a new `queued` count across all projects. The statusline (`src/cli/statusline.ts:159,170`) reads `global`, not the pane's own counts, labelled as machine scope. `asking` counts workers waiting on main; it is not shown as owner load (owner requests come later). Claude, pi and Codex lines show the same numbers.

acceptance.text: Test (M2 Try, counts): jobs running in two projects and one queued give the same running/queued in two panes' statuslines; starting the queued job changes both
Test: a pane with no own jobs still shows the machine counts

tickets.title: Local CPU and RAM in the statusline
tickets.what: Spec §5 M2. Show local CPU% and RAM (Linux/WSL guest, labelled as such) in the statuslines without blocking. CPU% needs a persisted prior `/proc/stat` sample, because each `hud statusline` call is a fresh process: keep one small sample file under `$HUD_HOME` and compute the delta; the first call after a gap shows no CPU% rather than a guess. RAM from `/proc/meminfo` (MemAvailable); add swap only when it is under pressure. No host (Windows) metrics.

acceptance.text: Test: two calls with synthetic `/proc/stat` samples give the expected CPU%; a missing or stale sample shows no CPU%
Test: RAM from a synthetic meminfo; swap appears only above the pressure threshold
Measured: statusline wall time stays within its current budget (number in the report)
